doc.name: A — eyewear catalogue, archive shelving, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: titanium optical frames
Category: eyewear
Shot programme: archive shelving
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the visual lead responsible for this eyewear product library. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the floating levitation in an archive shelving treatment.

SUBJECT. A titanium optical frames. Treat the attached reference as the single source of truth for the product's geometry, proportion, colourway, finish and label typography. Do not redesign, restyle, re-letter or embellish it.

CAMERA. Product suspended mid-air with no visible support and a soft drop shadow beneath. Shoot on a probe macro lens at f/2, framing for rule-of-thirds weighting to frame-right.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with split gel lighting, teal on the shadow side and magenta on the key side. Stage the product on or against fine sand, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a low-key grade holding detail in the deepest shadows only. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

SUBJECT. A titanium optical frames. Lock the product itself to the reference — no proportional drift, no invented branding, no cleaned-up typography. Everything else in the frame is your design decision.

CAMERA. Product with two colourway or size siblings in stepped depth. Shoot on a 20mm wide at f/8, framing for a stacked layered composition with three depth planes.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a book light bounce producing an extremely soft wrap. Stage the product on or against wet terrazzo, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a bleach-bypass look with crushed saturation and lifted contrast. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Return ONE image-generation prompt as a single unbroken paragraph. No preamble, no headings, no bullet points, no commentary, no markdown.
